subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should CLI health/status/stability avoid direct shared-state DB WAL maintenance while a gateway is running via RPC-first read-only fallback, or should OpenClaw add an explicit single-writer gateway lease first?
rationale: Both directions can address the reported data-loss class, but the choice changes CLI observability, doctor migration timing, gateway ownership, and recovery behavior for a shared persisted store.

options.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Make diagnostic commands use the running gateway when available and permit only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file fallback while a gateway owns the DB.

options.title: Single-writer lease first
options.body: Have the gateway own write and WAL-maintenance access through an explicit lease, with other processes refusing writer-style shared DB opens while it is held.

options.title: Forensics before contract change
options.body: Wait for the sanitized corrupt DB bundle and a throwaway runtime harness before choosing the DB ownership fix shape.

recommendation.title: RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Make diagnostic commands use the running gateway when available and permit only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file fallback while a gateway owns the DB.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for shared SQLite ownership is the shared state DB introduction, and this decision needs the owner of the DB/gateway contract.
